newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Communists to discuss joining cabinet.
newsitem.headline: French Communists to discuss joining cabinet.

text.p: French Communist leader Robert Hue said on Sunday he would discuss with Socialist leader Lionel Jospin his party's possible participation in a government following the left's election victory.

"The Communist Party's approach aims at participating in the government of France...We will assume our responsibilities," he said. "I have made proposals to Lionel Jospin, I want these to be discussed and I believe we can move forward," he said on television.

It was not yet clear whether the Socialists would need Communist votes for a National Assembly majority. The Communist leadership is divided on whether to join a cabinet, support it from outside, or remain on the sidelines and back it on a case-by-case basis.
Asked whether the Communists would join the cabinet, Hue said: "All that is open, we will discuss it." He said he had talked to Jospin earlier in the evening.

In last-minute pre-election talks with Jospin, Hue had set conditions for joining a left-wing cabinet, seeking assurances that it would rapidly raise salaries and order new taxes on investment earnings.

Jospin has said his cabinet would be pluralistic and include ministers from various parties so as to reflect the election alliance between Socialists, Communists and Greens. But aides have said he would not accept any conditions from the Communists.
